label: epa-vs-statbotics
armDescription: Measured with --warmup 2016-2020: those seasons are replayed to warm carried EPA state and are never reported on. Matches how `compare:epa-statbotics` invokes the script.
rationale: RE-BASELINED 2026-09-11 ONTO THE WARM ARM (todo epa-statbotics-check-baseline-is-cold-arm, decided by the developer).  WHICH ARM THIS FILE DESCRIBES -- the omission that made the previous drift invisible, now stated as data in `arm` and `warmupSeasons` above, not only in prose: these bands were measured with `--warmup 2016-2020`, i.e. 2016-2020 are replayed ONLY to warm the carried EPA state and are never reported on. That is exactly how `compare:epa-statbotics` invokes the script, so the gate and the npm script now describe the same arm and cannot silently diverge again.  WHY: quick task 260911-r7e added `--warmup 2016-2020` to `compare:epa-statbotics`. The previous bands were measured on the COLD arm, which cold-started every team in 2022 while the Statbotics column it was differenced against held its real 2019/2020 carry-in -- the same artefact that made the published methodology page understate our own 2022 accuracy by ~2.2 pp. Leaving cold bands in place while the script runs warm meant `--check` was comparing warm statistics against a cold record.  MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: `--check` PASSED against the OLD cold bands under the warm arm before this re-baseline (2026-09-11). The drift was therefore a LATENT mislabel, not an active false-fail -- the cold bands were wide enough (+/-0.05 slope/pearson, +/-1.0 mad) to absorb the arm change. This file is being corrected because it named the wrong arm and was stamped with a three-versions-stale `algorithmVersion`, not because a gate was firing. Recorded so a later reader does not infer a regression that never happened.  HALF-WIDTH FORMULA IS UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-04 bands: slope/pearson +/-0.05, meanAbsoluteDifference +/-1.0 points, both standard deviations +/-max(1.5, 10% of the measured value) so a large-point-scale season (2026: ourSD ~51) is not gated by an absolute band sized for a small-scale one (2022: ourSD ~10). No half-width grew. Bands remain centred on the measured value of the `minMatchesFiltered` arm (>=12 matches): low-match teams are noisy on both sides and would otherwise dominate meanAbsoluteDifference (see docs/models/epa-vs-statbotics.md).  The computation is deterministic (no randomness in the aggregate statistics), so re-running the script unchanged reproduces these figures exactly -- the bands exist to catch a REAL regression in EPA's attribution arithmetic or component extraction, not measurement noise.  KNOWN LIMITATION, carried forward from the 2026-09-04 record and still true: 2026 is an in-progress season. Its row will need re-measuring as more of it is played and both our EPA state and Statbotics' team-year figures shift. That is a named limitation of gating a live season, not an oversight.
